original_question: Do there exist a profinite group G, a field k of characteristic p > 0, and a finite-dimensional continuous k-linear representation V of G with End_k(V) = k such that the universal deformation ring R(G, V) is Noetherian but is not a local complete intersection?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Question 2.1, "Can deformation rings of group representations not be local complete intersections?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s existential problem: it asks for a profinite group G, a positive-characteristic coefficient field k, a finite-dimensional continuous k-linear representation V, and whether the associated universal deformation ring R(G,V) can be Noetherian without being a local complete intersection.
missing_details: The paper assumes k is a perfect field of characteristic p>0, not just an arbitrary field of characteristic p>0.
V is not just a representation abstractly; it is a finite-dimensional k-vector space equipped with the discrete topology and a continuous k-linear action of G.
The endomorphism hypothesis in the paper is End_{kG}(V)=k, not End_k(V)=k.
The notation R(G,V) is taken in the standard deformation-theoretic sense with auxiliary coefficient ring O chosen to be the ring W(k) of infinite Witt vectors over k.
The official formulation asks for G and V "as above," so those setup hypotheses must be imported explicitly to make the question stand-alone.

Immediately after Question 2.1, the paper notes that the Noetherian condition is equivalent to dim_k H^1(G,End_k(V))<∞; this is relevant nearby context even though it is not built into the official question statement.
refined_question: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p>0, let G be a profinite group, and let V be a finite-dimensional k-vector space with the discrete topology, equipped with a continuous k-linear action of G such that End_{kG}(V)=k. If R(G,V) denotes the universal deformation ring of V over W(k), the ring of infinite Witt vectors over k, does there exist such a triple (G,k,V) for which R(G,V) is Noetherian but not a local complete intersection?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Chinburg’s one-page problem note in Section 2, and the nearest official formulation is exactly Question 2.1 on page 135. The surrounding paragraph supplies the hypotheses that make the question precise and paper-faithful: k is perfect of characteristic p>0, V is a discrete finite-dimensional k-vector space with continuous G-action, End_{kG}(V)=k, and the deformation theory is taken over W(k). Your draft preserves the main existential structure and conclusion, but it misses the perfectness of k, omits the discrete-topology clause, and most importantly replaces the paper’s Schur-type condition End_{kG}(V)=k by the much stronger and incorrect End_k(V)=k. The note after Question 2.1 adds the nearby reformulation of Noetherianity via H^1, which explains the scope of the question but does not replace the official statement.
